name: OCR GCSE Computer Science (J277)
subject: Computer Science
topic_note: The topic numbers match the filters in Smartrevise, so you can practise questions on exactly the topics you need.

topics.name: Architecture of the CPU
revise: The fetch-execute cycle, step by step: what moves between RAM and the CPU.
What the MAR, MDR, program counter and accumulator each hold.
What the ALU, control unit and cache do.
videos: The purpose of the CPU: the fetch-execute cycle

topics.name: CPU performance
revise: How clock speed, cache size and number of cores each affect performance.
Why doubling the cores does not always double the speed.

topics.name: Embedded systems
revise: What an embedded system is: a computer inside a larger device with one job.
Examples, and why they are cheap, small and reliable.

topics.name: Primary storage (memory)
revise: Why computers need primary storage.
RAM and ROM: what each holds and whether it is volatile.
Virtual memory: what it is and why it slows the computer down.

topics.name: Secondary storage
revise: Optical, magnetic and solid state storage, with an example of each.
Compare them on capacity, speed, portability, durability, reliability and cost.
Choose a suitable device for a scenario and explain why.

topics.name: Units
revise: Bit, nibble, byte, kilobyte up to petabyte, and that each step is 1000 (or 1024).
Work out file sizes for sound, images and text, and how many files fit on a device.

topics.name: Data storage
revise: Convert between denary, 8-bit binary and hexadecimal; add binary and spot overflow.
Binary shifts, character sets (ASCII, Unicode), images (resolution, colour depth, metadata).
Sound: how sample rate and bit depth affect quality and file size.

topics.name: Compression
revise: Why files are compressed.
Lossy and lossless compression: how they differ and when to use each.

topics.name: Networks and topologies
revise: LAN and WAN, and the factors that affect network performance.
Client-server and peer-to-peer, and the hardware needed to build a LAN.
Star and mesh topologies: draw them and give pros and cons.
videos: Factors that affect the performance of networks

topics.name: Wired and wireless networks, protocols and layers
revise: Ethernet, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and why wireless networks are encrypted.
IP and MAC addresses, standards, and what each common protocol is for.
The idea of layers and why they help.
videos: Modes of connection: wired and wireless
The use of IP and MAC addressing

topics.name: Threats to computer systems and networks
revise: Malware, social engineering (including phishing), brute-force and denial of service attacks.
Data interception and SQL injection: how each works and what it can do.

topics.name: Identifying and preventing vulnerabilities
revise: Penetration testing, anti-malware, firewalls, user access levels and passwords.
Encryption and physical security: match each defence to the threat it stops.

topics.name: Operating systems
revise: The user interface, memory management and multitasking.
Peripheral management and drivers, user management and file management.
videos: The purpose and functionality of operating systems

topics.name: Utility software
revise: Encryption software, defragmentation and data compression.
Explain why defragmentation makes a hard disk faster: the parts of a file end up together.

topics.name: Ethical, legal, cultural and environmental impact
revise: Ethical, legal, cultural, environmental and privacy issues, with examples.
The Data Protection Act 2018, Computer Misuse Act 1990, Copyright Designs and Patents Act 1988.
Open source and proprietary software.
videos: Impacts of digital technology on wider society

topics.name: Computational thinking
revise: Abstraction, decomposition and algorithmic thinking, with an example of each.

topics.name: Designing, creating and refining algorithms
revise: Inputs, processes and outputs; structure diagrams.
Pseudocode and flowcharts, and finding and fixing errors in algorithms.
Trace tables: one row for each change, every pass of the loop.

topics.name: Searching and sorting algorithms
revise: Binary and linear search: the steps, and when binary search can be used.
Bubble, merge and insertion sort: show every stage, not just the final list.

topics.name: Programming fundamentals
revise: Variables, constants, inputs, outputs and assignment.
Sequence, selection and iteration (count- and condition-controlled loops).
Arithmetic, comparison and Boolean operators, including MOD and DIV.
videos: Variables, constants, inputs, outputs and assignments

topics.name: Data types
revise: Integer, real, Boolean, character and string: choose the right one for some data.
Casting: changing one data type into another, e.g. int("5").

topics.name: Additional programming techniques
revise: String handling, file handling, and records.
1D and 2D arrays: a loop inside a loop to read array[x, y].
SQL SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE; functions and procedures with parameters; random numbers.

topics.name: Defensive design
revise: Anticipating misuse, authentication and input validation.
Maintainability: comments, sensible names, indentation and sub programs.

topics.name: Testing
revise: Iterative and final testing.
Syntax and logic errors: spot and fix them.
Normal, boundary, invalid and erroneous test data, with examples.
videos: The purpose and types of testing
Refining algorithms to make them more robust

topics.name: Boolean logic
revise: AND, OR and NOT gates: symbols and truth tables.
Combine gates into logic diagrams and complete their truth tables.
videos: Applying logical operators in truth tables

topics.name: Languages
revise: High-level and low-level languages: features and when to use each.
Translators: compilers, interpreters and assemblers, and how they differ.

topics.name: The Integrated Development Environment (IDE)
revise: IDE tools: editor, error diagnostics, run-time environment and translators.
